findings.title: strip-quoted-strings false-positive suppression has zero test coverage
findings.description: Both block-rm-rf.sh and safety-block.sh strip quoted strings before pattern matching (the sed lines that remove double and single quoted content). The tests only feed raw dangerous commands or safe commands. No test exercises the false-positive case: a command like echo "dangerous pattern inside quotes" where the dangerous pattern is inside quotes and should NOT trigger a block. Without this, the strip logic could be removed or inverted and every existing test would still pass.
findings.suggested_test: Add test: bash hooks/safety-block.sh <<< json-with-command-containing-quoted-rm-rf; assert exit 0. Mirror for block-rm-rf.sh.

findings.title: log-tool-calls.sh post event never invoked in any test
findings.description: test-hooks.sh calls log-tool-calls.sh pre twice but never calls log-tool-calls.sh post. The post branch of log_tool_call.py (lines 193-251) is a completely separate code path: it reads the pair temp file, computes duration_ms, extracts exit_status from tool_response, and emits event=post. None of this fires. The test cannot catch regressions to: pair-file lookup, duration calculation, exit_status extraction, output redaction on post, or the _raw fallback for non-dict tool_response.
findings.suggested_test: Add a fixture with tool_response field. Call pre then post with same session_id/tool_input, read last line of JSONL, assert event==post and duration_ms >= 0 and exit_status == 0.

findings.title: Pre/Post pair-file pairing mechanism never round-tripped under test
findings.description: The pre/post pairing (temp file keyed by sha256 of session_id+tool_input) is the mechanism that isolates duration_ms per-call and prevents cross-session pollution. The PR context notes this was a bug caught during smoke testing. No test fires a matched pre+post pair and asserts the pair file is created, read, and deleted. No test verifies that two concurrent sessions with different session_ids do not share pair files. The fallback glob path (when pair file is missing) is completely unexercised.
findings.suggested_test: Test 1: pre then post with same fixture, assert pair temp file is created after pre and deleted after post. Test 2: fire pre for two sessions, fire post for session 1, assert session 2 pair file is not consumed. Test 3: fire post without prior pre, assert duration_ms==0 and no crash.

findings.title: Six of seven safety-block.sh patterns have no test coverage
findings.description: safety-block.sh implements 7 distinct block patterns. Only the rm-rf-against-/Users pattern is tested (via tool-input-bash-rmrf.json). The following patterns added in this PR have no test at all: sudo rm-rf any target, dd of=/dev/disk*, mkfs/wipefs, fork bomb, chmod -R 777 against root or home, force-push to protected branch. Any of these patterns could be deleted, inverted, or have a regex bug without failing any test.
findings.suggested_test: Add inline heredoc tests for each pattern asserting exit 2: sudo rm -rf /var, dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/disk0, mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda, the fork bomb pattern, chmod -R 777 /, git push --force origin main. Also test git push origin --force and git push -f to cover variant ordering.

findings.title: Redaction tests only cover redact.py; log_tool_call.py carries a duplicate pattern set with no independent test
findings.description: log_tool_call.py contains an inline copy of all redaction patterns commented kept-in-sync-with-redact.py. test-redaction.sh tests only redact.py. If the inline copy in log_tool_call.py drifts (e.g. a pattern is updated in redact.py but not in log_tool_call.py), the redaction tests will pass while the logger silently leaks secrets. The Authorization-header partial-leak fix was applied to both files, but the test harness provides no protection against future drift.
findings.suggested_test: Add a test that pipes a secret-bearing JSON directly through log-tool-calls.sh pre and reads the resulting JSONL line, asserting the redaction marker is present and the raw secret is absent in the logged output.

findings.title: mustnot check for GH token uses 9-char prefix rather than full token
findings.description: In test-redaction.sh line 18, the mustnot value for the GitHub token case is ghp_aaaaaaaaa (9 chars of the 40-char token). The grep -qF check would pass even if redaction only suppressed the last 31 characters while leaving the first 9 in the output. A correct assertion would use the full token value or a sufficiently long unambiguous suffix to confirm complete removal.

findings.title: ENOSPC error path in log_tool_call.py has no test
findings.description: log_tool_call.py explicitly catches errno.ENOSPC in _atomic_append and returns 0, a hard invariant per the PR context (logging must never break a tool call). No test simulates disk-full conditions and asserts exit 0. The code path is reachable but entirely unexercised.

residual_risks: The post-event duration_ms field could silently be 0 for all real calls if the pair file is never found, without any test failing — a data quality regression invisible to the test suite.

If log_tool_call.py receives a non-dict tool_response that fails the _raw wrapping in an unexpected way, the outer try/except in __main__ catches it but the test suite never exercises this path to confirm the invariant holds.

test-settings-valid.sh checks that hook script files referenced in settings.json exist on disk, but does not verify that symlinks installed by install.sh point to the correct repo file — a dangling symlink would pass the file-existence check.
testing_gaps: No test for log-tool-calls.sh post mode — the majority of log_tool_call.py is unreachable by the test suite
No test for pre+post pairing round-trip (pair file creation, reading, and deletion lifecycle)
No test for strip-quoted-strings false-positive suppression in safety-block.sh or block-rm-rf.sh
No tests for 6 of 7 safety-block.sh patterns (sudo rm-rf, dd to disk, mkfs/wipefs, fork bomb, chmod 777, force-push)
No end-to-end test asserting redaction works through log_tool_call.py — only redact.py is exercised
No test for the fallback glob path in post-event pair lookup (when pair file was not created)
No concurrent-session isolation test confirming pair file keying separates sessions correctly
